title: Reporting, Data and Analytics Platform: Management Console, Dashboards, KPI/SLA Reporting, Data Warehouse, Ad-Hoc Query, Audit-Log Retention and Fraud-Monitoring Analytics
capability_statement:
Parsons delivers an end-to-end Reporting, Data and Analytics platform purpose-built for inspection programs, anchored on a central inspection-data infrastructure (referred to as the VIID on a comparable I/M Program) that serves as the canonical data warehouse for all program-related information - including specified vehicle data from the contracting agency's files, prior I/M test information, sticker information, station/inspector/repair-technician information, Technical Service Bulletins, Master Reference Tables, manufacturer recall information, administrative files, calibration data, oversight data, and station/inspector certification information (chunks 2074, 2079). The infrastructure is architected in the AWS cloud with multi-AZ Aurora MySQL (six-way replication across availability zones, fault-tolerant to loss of two data copies), highly available S3 object storage (six-way replication used for static front-end content, data archiving, and logging data), AWS Fargate for application microservices with auto-scaling and resiliency patterns, Route 53 DNS, AWS WAF and AWS Shield Firewall protections, CloudFront edge caching with TLS encryption, network segmentation via VPC with NACLs, and a load balancer distributing traffic across two active availability zones (chunks 2062, 2063). The reporting tier consists of a Pentaho ad-hoc reporting service running on EC2 autoscaling groups with failover and auto-recovery, plus AWS QuickSight as a resilient Business Intelligence service that can leverage ML technologies and operates with high availability across multiple AZs (chunk 2063).

State personnel and authorized users access the system through a Management Console and secure web portals over the public internet using secure protocols, while inspection test units access the same data infrastructure via secure web services and Parsons' operations team manages the system via encrypted channels (chunk 2062). The reporting suite supports a user-friendly, web-based interface; role-based security; formatting, filtering, sorting, grouping, aggregations, and summary calculations; presentation of data in crosstab reports, grids, and charts; web-based dashboards for a quick view of key performance indicators; data drill-down features supporting root-cause analysis inquiry; report scheduling; web and email report sharing; and data export to PDF, CSV, and MS Excel (chunks 2067, 2068, 2070). Authorized state staff (six users on a comparable I/M Program) have direct access to the data to run reports, with on-demand training and ongoing support for searching, navigating, and accessing the data; written analyses of queries used in ad-hoc reports are supplied on request (chunk 2069). The system provides predefined management reports and ad-hoc reporting capabilities, with a job scheduler, a report library cataloging report purpose and usage, and exports to PDF, Excel, RTF, HTML, and plain text in conformance with RFP requirements (chunks 2050, 2068, 2069). Data is pushed to the contracting agency's downstream systems via batch or web-service API to load into the agency's system or data warehouse where an API is available (chunk 2069).

KPI/SLA reporting is delivered through a dedicated Service Level Tracking Application (SLTA) hosted in AWS on a comparable I/M Program. The SLTA provides a summary of all SLAs stated in the RFP, identifies delivery of each required task, and provides the contracting agency with a way to ensure contractual obligations are met (chunk 1965). Additional periodic reporting cadence includes weekly progress reports, monthly status reports (including operational minutes available and outage/downtime minutes for the previous month, with agency-approved downtime distinguished on a comparable program), monthly and annual reports, semi-annual recommendations reports, and the annual EPA report - all governed by approved templates and procedures with the ability to accommodate frequency, content, and format changes throughout the contract term (chunks 1957, 2024, 2088). On the comparable I/M Program, audit data, oversight data, and contract-monitoring outputs are integrated into the dashboard suite so the agency can rapidly review covert audit emission records, covert audit reports, overt audit results, and station/inspector performance.

Fraud-monitoring analytics are a first-class capability. The system collects, processes, and analyzes data to support management and compliance programs directed at eliminating fraud and noncompliance in emissions-related inspections and repairs. Parsons' fraud-prevention technique uses analytic audit triggers to detect data anomalies that identify potential incidents of fraudulent testing and repair, with experience drawn from comparable inspection programs continuously feeding improvements to the trigger library used to identify suspicious activity by stations and/or inspectors (chunks 2068, 2079). The reporting suite explicitly supports drill-down into anomalies in the data to help identify possible fraudulent activity at a station or by an inspector (chunk 2068). Parsons also supports collection of data from mobile remote sensing equipment via batch download or standard PC-based software permitting data manipulation and reporting (chunk 2080).

Audit-data retention and audit-logging are implemented across application, system, network, and security layers. The system maintains journal files (transaction journals) logging all system transactions; an automated journal/log records all add/change/delete activity and is archived for audit (chunks 1970, 2080). On a comparable I/M Program, all data is kept online for the life of the contract (exceeding the 27-month requirement) and is retrievable for 180 days after contract expiration; covert data, including covert audit emission records and covert audit reports, resides in the data infrastructure for 180 days after contract expiration (chunk 2067). Externally hosted system monitoring/audit-logging requirements are addressed through a dedicated controls area on the comparable program, supported by quarterly internal and external vulnerability tests, security assessments during and after critical system changes, and an established cybersecurity practice that integrates antivirus/malware controls, firewall control and intrusion detection, database safeguarding, OS hardening, and secure communication transmissions (chunks 1956, 1982, 1983). The system supports server-log review, stored-transaction availability to the contracting agency, and provision of logs and reports to the agency in agreed format - including latency statistics, user access, user-access IP address, user-access history, and security logs for all state data, with reports and logs maintained for the contract term and two years after conclusion (mapped to RFP R-021/R-022).

Program-evaluation and oversight reporting is a distinct workstream that funnels into the data warehouse. On a comparable I/M Program, Parsons' overt audit, covert audit, remote records audit, and remote visual audit programs feed structured findings into the central data infrastructure, where they are surfaced through dashboards, scheduled reports, and ad-hoc queries; an electronic audit application (touchscreen laptops with electronic signature capture and direct integration to the data warehouse) eliminated paper overt-audit reports submitted to the contracting agency (chunk 1973). Real-time data auditing with emissions test interruption is delivered as part of the comprehensive reporting and data-management offering (chunk 1984). Supporting capabilities for externally hosted IT requirements - regulatory compliance verification, CONUS access controls, SOC reports, accessibility, capacity, identity and access management - are integrated with the reporting platform on the comparable program (chunks 1955, 1956).

differentiators:
- **Purpose-built I/M central data infrastructure as the system of record**: The VIID-equivalent serves as the canonical repository for vehicle data, prior test data, sticker and station/inspector data, TSBs, MRTs, manufacturer recall data, calibration data, oversight data, certification information, and administrative files - a single warehouse that anchors all reporting, dashboards, and ad-hoc query rather than a bolted-on reporting layer (chunks 2074, 2079).
- **Two-tier reporting platform - Pentaho ad-hoc plus AWS QuickSight BI**: The reporting tier deliberately separates ad-hoc query (Pentaho on EC2 autoscaling with failover) from dashboard/BI (QuickSight, resilient and ML-capable across multiple AZs), giving power users self-service query and executives KPI dashboards without compromising either workload (chunk 2063).
- **Service Level Tracking Application (SLTA) hosted in AWS**: A dedicated SLA-tracking application that summarizes contractual SLAs, identifies delivery of each task, and gives the contracting agency a continuously available view of contractual performance - introduced as part of Parsons' compliance commitment on a comparable I/M Program (chunk 1965).
- **Direct agency-staff ad-hoc query with training and written-analysis support**: Six direct data-access seats with on-demand training and written analysis of queries used in ad-hoc reports on request, beyond just self-service tools (chunk 2069).
- **Analytic fraud-detection triggers fed by multi-program experience**: Fraud-prevention analytic audit triggers in the reporting suite are continuously improved using cross-program experience from comparable I/M programs, identifying suspicious activity by stations and/or inspectors with drill-down into anomalies (chunks 2068, 2079).
- **Covert audit data integrated into the warehouse with retention guarantees**: Covert audit emission records and covert audit reports reside in the central data infrastructure for 180 days after contract expiration; an electronic audit application with touchscreen laptops, electronic signature capture, and warehouse integration eliminates paper audit submissions (chunks 1973, 2067).
- **Defined push-to-agency data interface**: Data is pushed to the contracting agency's downstream system or data warehouse via batch or web-service API, providing a clear NGV-ODS-equivalent integration path rather than relying on the agency to pull from operational systems (chunk 2069).
- **Agency-grade reporting cadence governed by approved templates**: Weekly progress, monthly, semi-annual recommendations, annual, and Annual EPA reports - with the explicit ability to accommodate changes in frequency, content, and format throughout the contract term using Parsons' approved templates and procedures (chunks 1957, 2024).
- **Inspection-volume and uptime reporting baked into monthly cadence**: Monthly report includes operational minutes available and outage/downtime minutes for the previous month, with agency-approved downtime distinguished, supporting SLA accountability (chunk 2088).
- **Cloud-grade durability for audit logs**: Audit logs and archived journals stored in S3 with up to six-way replication and Aurora multi-AZ database with six-way replication tolerating loss of up to two copies, ensuring audit-data integrity and 24/7/365 availability (chunk 2063).
- **Real-time data auditing with emissions test interruption**: Delivered as part of comprehensive program-management services, allowing the data and analytics platform to act on suspicious activity in flight, not just retrospectively (chunk 1984).
gap_notes:
- **Two requirements in the bundle reference state-specific systems and processes that are out of scope for this neutralized synthesis.** R-068 (Conform to NJ VIIS-Reporting System Specification Version 0.2, dated June 19, 2009) is a state-specific specification compliance commitment - the proposal must affirm conformance, but the evidence does not describe prior conformance to that specific specification. Treat R-068 as a forward-looking compliance commitment.
- **R-011 (Monitor NJSTART for Bid Amendments) and A-024/A-025/A-021 (NJ-specific ethics/contribution reporting) are procurement-process and ethics obligations, not Reporting/Data/Analytics platform requirements.** No data-platform past performance is needed; the proposal team should route these to the procurement and legal sections.
- **Several requirements bundled into Theme 4 are facilities/maintenance reporting obligations rather than Reporting/Data/Analytics platform features.** R-048 (monthly written complaint report to SCM), V-007 / A-052 / A-065 / A-069 / A-070 (CIF maintenance and repairs report formats and sort orders), R-019 (audit-report response with corrective action plan), R-036 (written report of staffing retention efforts), and A-085 (stored transactions and logs available to State) describe specific operational reports the contractor will produce. The Reporting/Data/Analytics platform supports producing these reports (predefined management reports, scheduled reports, ad-hoc query, multi-format export), but the evidence does not include sample CIF maintenance reports, complaint reports, or staffing-retention reports from comparable programs in the bundle. Capture team should pair these with the facilities-maintenance and contract-management workstreams.
- **A-101 (report library with purpose/usage), A-103 (job scheduler for reports), A-106 (export to PDF/Excel/RTF/HTML/plain text), A-018 (describe how tasks are performed/monitored/tracked), A-035/A-036 (automated journal/log for add/change/delete; archive/store log activities for audit), A-112 (maintain log of users), A-002 (review server logs)**: These are directly supported by the reporting suite and journal/log capabilities described in chunks 2050, 2068-2070, 2080. The evidence covers PDF/CSV/Excel; RTF, HTML, and plain-text export are RFP-required and the proposal should confirm support of those additional formats.
- **A-028 (privileged-account controls and MFA), A-056 (audit logging and continuous log review), A-057 (standard issued device security configuration), A-061 (ICS/SCADA/OT controls), A-030/R-015/R-020/R-021 (defense-in-depth, continuous monitoring, monitoring/alerting/logging description), R-033 (vulnerability monitoring of dependencies), R-037 (web application protective technologies), R-060 (physical-access security monitoring), A-010 (incident response capability), R-002/R-017/R-021/R-022/R-024 (security incident reporting in 24 hours, secure data disposal, security logs/reports format, log/report retention, annual data center audit), A-013/A-014 (covered-telecommunications equipment prohibitions), A-008/R-043 (encryption-failure breach-cost responsibility), A-024/A-005/A-002 (Clean Air/Water Act and Personal Data definitions), R-011 (state file transfer methodology)**: These are security/compliance controls that touch on the Reporting/Data/Analytics platform (audit logging, log review, incident reporting). The evidence describes Parsons' cybersecurity practice (chunks 1982, 1983), AWS WAF and AWS Shield (chunk 2062), and SOC 2 audit (referenced indirectly via Attachment G in chunk 1960) but is not exhaustive on each specific control. Many of these are cross-referenced in Theme 18 and Theme 5/6 (Security and Privacy). For Theme 4 we focus on the reporting/audit-log/dashboard implications; the deeper control responses belong to the security themes.
- **A-085 (stored transactions and logs available to State)**: Directly supported by chunks 2074, 2080 (transaction journals, automated journal/log for add/change/delete) and chunk 2067 (online retention). Restated as a data-platform commitment in the capability statement.
- **R-068 (Conform to NJ VIIS-Reporting System Specification Version 0.2 dated June 19, 2009)**: No evidence of prior conformance to that specific specification document; capture team should verify the specification with the contracting agency and tailor the data dictionary, file formats, and reporting-system interfaces accordingly. The Pentaho/QuickSight reporting tier and the batch/web-service API push capability (chunk 2069) provide a sound foundation for conforming.
- **A-103 (job scheduler) and A-101 (report library with purpose/usage)**: Reporting-suite features bullet-listed in chunks 2068-2071 explicitly mention 'Report scheduling' and the broader reporting-tool catalogue; the proposal should confirm a documented report-library deliverable with purpose-of-use metadata for each report.
- **A-106 (export formats)**: Evidence explicitly cites PDF, CSV, and MS Excel (chunk 2070). RTF, HTML, and plain text are RFP-required and should be confirmed as supported by the reporting-tool stack (Pentaho is known to support these formats in standard configurations, but the evidence does not state this explicitly).
- **R-097 (designate a QA Manager) and A-028 (limited ITS access via Management Console)**: Organizational obligations and access-control commitments. The Management Console is referenced indirectly via state-personnel access through portals/reporting/ad-hoc query (chunk 2062), but evidence does not describe a 'limited ITS access via Management Console for SCM-approved personnel' configuration in the same wording. Forward-looking commitment.
- **Voice and naming**: Per instructions, all references to specific past-performance jurisdictions are neutralized as 'a comparable I/M Program,' 'a comparable State Vehicle Inspection Program,' 'a comparable Heavy-Duty Emissions Program,' or 'a comparable State Electronic Periodic Motor Vehicle Inspection Program.' Underlying source chunks (e.g., 1965, 1973, 1988, 1989, 1991, 1993) reference specific agency names; capture team should rely on those chunks for verifiable past-performance citations while keeping the customer-facing capability statement neutralized.
